items.alt_text: "3D rendering of a light gray, wooden sculpture of a house with arms and legs sitting on a stump holding a staff."
creator: Brouwer, Charlie, 1946 -
description: A sculpture from the "Homebodies" series of sculptures featuring  figures with human appendages and house-shaped torsos. This sculpture is a house with arms and legs sitting on a stump and holding a staff.
subject: Sculpture
Wood sculpture
Art
items.title: At Home in the Woods
items.visual_description: "A fifteen foot tall sculpture of a house with human arms and legs seated on a stump. The base is 3 feet by 4 feet and outlines the shape of the stump and feet. The figure holds a tall staff in the right hand with the left hand resting on the left knee. The house is made of wide, horizontal pieces of wood. The arms and legs are made of longer, thin pieces of wood with carved hands and shoes. The stump is made of wide vertical pieces of wood. The staff is a long branch. The sculpture is grey with natural green tints from exposure to the elements."

items.alt_text: "3D rendering of a light gray, wooden sculpture of a house with arms and legs sitting on a stump holding a staff."
creator: Brouwer, Charlie, 1946 -
description: A sculpture from the "Homebodies" series of sculptures featuring  figures with human appendages and house-shaped torsos. This sculpture is a house with arms and legs sitting on a stump and holding a staff.
subject: Sculpture
Wood sculpture
Art
items.title: At Home in the Woods
items.visual_description: "A fifteen foot tall sculpture of a house with human arms and legs seated on a stump. The base is 3 feet by 4 feet and outlines the shape of the stump and feet. The figure holds a tall staff in the right hand with the left hand resting on the left knee. The house is made of wide, horizontal pieces of wood. The arms and legs are made of longer, thin pieces of wood with carved hands and shoes. The stump is made of wide vertical pieces of wood. The staff is a long branch. The sculpture is grey with natural green tints from exposure to the elements."

items.alt_text: "3D rendering of a light gray, wooden sculpture of a house with legs standing upright."
creator: Brouwer, Charlie, 1946 -
description: A sculpture from the "Homebodies" series of sculptures featuring  figures with human appendages and house-shaped torsos. This sculpture is a house standing upright on two legs.
subject: Sculpture
Wood sculpture
Art
items.title: Being Home
items.visual_description: "A sixteen foot tall sculpture of a house with human legs standing on a two foot by three foot pentagon-shaped base. The house is made of wide, horizontal pieces of wood. The legs are made of longer pieces of wood patchworked together with circular shapes at the knees and shoes. The sculpture is grey and stands upright with feet shoulder width apart.\n"

items.alt_text: "3D rendering of a blue, wooden sculpture covered in white stars of a figure with a hat standing and looking up."
creator: Brouwer, Charlie, 1946 -
description: A sculpture from the "All Over the Place" series of sculptures originally placed in numerous locations around the New River Valley. This sculpture has sat near the Calfee Community and Cultural Center in Pulaski, Virginia and now resides on the "Out There" Sculpture Trail in Floyd, Virginia. The piece was inspired by the spiritual song "My Lord, What a Morning.
subject: Sculpture
Wood sculpture
Art
items.title: When the Stars Begin to Fall
items.visual_description: "A seven foot tall sculpture of a man wearing a hat and standing on a three foot wide circular base. The sculpture is made of different sizes and shapes of locust wood pieces with longer strips of wood for the legs, arms, and torso and circular pieces for the knees, hands, and head. The patchworked pieces show distinct textures. The sculpture is a dark blue that has faded from exposure to the elements and is dotted with white stars that are 3-4 inches long. The figure is standing and looking up at the sky with slightly bent knees and feet shoulder width apart. The left arm is extended slightly in front and the right is extended slightly behind the torso.\n"
